title: Incident review: connected AD activity
subtitle: Independent analysis of recorded emulation
author: Don Lopez
summary: Seven distinct-account failures, five successful RC4 service-ticket requests and IPC$/srvsvc checks precede GUID-linked remote PowerShell on three targets. The connected activity warrants authorization and command review. Authorized emulation or administration remains a competing explanation; business impact is not established.
scope: THESHIRE\pgustavo on WORKSTATION5; target records on WORKSTATION6, WORKSTATION7 and MORDORDC. Coverage: 25,993 host events and 1,121 packets; 226 host records selected. These are observed hosts, not confirmed compromised systems.

timeline.text: Seven failures share caller host, PID and session. Failure records have no client IP.
Five successful RC4 service tickets; IPC$/srvsvc checks span three hosts. Neither proves cracking or file theft.
Three wsmprovhost.exe / powershell.exe parent-child pairs have same-host GUID and account/session joins.

decisions.title: Correlate, with a causality limit
decisions.text: Matching TCP/5985 tuples corroborate client flows (for example H03882 / P00872). No end-to-end request ID proves a packet caused a particular PowerShell child.

decisions.title: Use execution time
decisions.text: The DC child executed at 08:29:58.095 UTC; collection at 08:30:37.907 UTC was 39.812 seconds later. This is collection delay, not a second execution wave.

recommendations.title: SOC analyst / establish authorization
recommendations.text: Check operator identity, change approval and full command/script-block content before assigning operational severity. Retain host, session and source references.

recommendations.title: Incident lead + system owner / conditional response
recommendations.text: If live evidence shows unauthorized ongoing activity, assess approved account/session restrictions and host isolation with the owner; preserve evidence and weigh service impact. No containment was performed in this historical review.

recommendations.title: Detection engineer / validate before deployment
recommendations.text: Baseline RC4 and WinRM use, test benign administration and late arrivals, then validate backend fields. Python analysis executed; the AD SPL/Sigma candidates remain unexecuted.

limits: OTRF recorded this PurpleSharp emulation in 2020; this is not a production incident or an owner-operated attack. Shared-password use, credential cracking, persistence, data theft and business impact remain unproven. Security timestamps use a calibrated capture-local UTC-04:00 assumption.
